about.title: Six and seven
about.length_note: About 10 minutes fits the material: two new numbers, 6 and 7, each shown on the five-frame, then a short mixed round of 0 to 7. Every beat stands alone, so you can stop after any beat and carry on later.

say.text: Welcome to class four: six and seven. There is no hurry. You can stop at any point and come back later.

show.text: Six and seven

say.text: First, a look at what we already know. This is a five-frame. It is a row of five boxes. When every box has one thing in it, we say the frame is full.

show.text: A row of five square boxes, each with one cup in it. The frame is completely full: 5 cups.

say.text: Let's count the cups together, touching each one: one, two, three, four, five. Five cups. The frame is full.

show.text: The same row of five cups, lit one at a time from left to right with the words 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 under them.

say.text: Your turn. Look at the full frame of cups. How many cups are there?

show.text: A full five-frame with 5 cups.

ask.q: How many cups are in the full frame?
ask.why: Every one of the five boxes has a cup, so the answer is 5. Counting one at a time gives the same answer.

say.text: Now something new. The five-frame is full, so we start a second row. We put one more cup just below the frame. Five and one more.

show.text: A full five-frame of 5 cups. Underneath, on its own, one extra cup. Label: 5 and 1 more.

say.text: Five and one more is six. Say it with me: six.
Here is the word and the digit together. Six is written with the digit 6. It has a curve that loops round at the bottom.

show.text: six = 6

say.text: Let's count six real things. For a grown-up: six keys on a table. For a child: six ducks on a pond. Touch each one and count: one, two, three, four, five, six.

show.text: Left: a five-frame full of keys with one more key underneath, 6 keys. Right: a five-frame full of ducks with one more duck underneath, 6 ducks.

say.text: Try one on your own. Look at the coins.

show.text: A full five-frame of coins with one extra coin below it.

ask.why: The frame holds 5 and there is 1 extra coin. Five and one more is 6.

say.text: Now we put five and six side by side. Five fills the frame and stops. Six fills the frame and spills over by one.

show.text: FIVE: a full frame, nothing underneath. | SIX: a full frame, plus 1 underneath.

say.text: Next, seven. Start with the full frame of five. This time we add two more underneath. Five and two more.

show.text: A full five-frame of 5 apples. Underneath, two extra apples side by side. Label: 5 and 2 more.

say.text: Five and two more is seven. Say it with me: seven.
The word is seven, and the digit is 7. It has a flat line across the top and a straight line coming down.

show.text: seven = 7

say.text: Count seven real things with me. A grown-up might have seven cups. A child might have seven apples. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.

show.text: A full five-frame of cups with two more cups underneath: 7 cups. Beside it, a full five-frame of apples with two more underneath: 7 apples.

say.text: Your turn. How many apples?

show.text: A full five-frame of apples with two extra apples underneath.

ask.why: The frame holds 5, and 2 more are underneath. Five and two more is 7.

say.text: Here is a quick way to tell them apart without counting every one. Five has nothing under the frame. Six has one under it. Seven has two under it.

show.text: 5: full frame, nothing under it | 6: full frame, 1 under it | 7: full frame, 2 under it

say.text: Let's use that. Look under the frame.

show.text: A full five-frame of balls with exactly one ball underneath.

ask.why: There is one ball under the full frame. Five and one more is 6.

say.text: Another one. This time, how many keys?

show.text: A full five-frame of keys with two keys underneath.

ask.why: Two keys sit under the full frame. Five and two more is 7.

say.text: Now let's mix in the numbers from earlier, including zero. Zero means nothing is there. Here is an empty frame.

show.text: A five-frame with all five boxes empty. Nothing under it.

ask.q: How many ducks are in the frame?
ask.why: No box has a duck in it, so there are none. Zero means nothing is there.

say.text: Here is a frame that is not full. Count the things inside it.

show.text: A five-frame with 3 coins in the first three boxes. The last two boxes are empty.

ask.why: Three boxes have a coin and two are empty, so there are 3.

say.text: One with no picture. Think of a full frame, then add two more.

show.text: 5 and 2 more = ?

ask.q: What is five and two more?
ask.why: Five and one more is 6, and one more again is 7. So five and two more is 7.

say.text: Well done. Today we met six, which is five and one more, and seven, which is five and two more. We saw the digits 6 and 7. We also practised telling 0 to 7 apart. Stop here, or have a break and come back.

show.text: 6 = five and 1 more | 7 = five and 2 more | 0 = nothing there
